name: delegate
description: Delegate a well-defined implementation task to a worker (an external coding-agent CLI such as GitHub Copilot CLI or Mistral Vibe). The work happens in an isolated git worktree on a dedicated branch: the main repo is NOT touched until you call apply. Asynchronous: returns a job_id immediately (you can launch several in parallel on independent parts, also on different workers). Use jobs to wait for / view the diff. Ideal for: boilerplate, tests, mechanical refactors, repetitive migrations, documentation, small features with a clear spec. Do NOT use it for architectural decisions or hard bugs.

task.description: Complete, self-contained spec: what to do, where, constraints. The worker cannot see your conversation.

files.description: Relevant files/folders (paths relative to the repo)

context.description: Useful context: conventions, APIs to use, existing examples to imitate

test_command.description: Command the worker must run to verify its work (e.g. 'npm test -- auth')

include_uncommitted.description: Start from the current state including uncommitted changes (default true). Untracked files are not included.

worker.description: Worker to use (see the workers tool). Omit it to use the session default or the configured preference order.

fallback.description: If the worker hits a quota/rate limit or its budget is used up, move on to the next worker (default: the fallback setting in the config).

model.description: Model for the chosen worker. For agy: a group (fast, standard, strong, frontier) or an exact slug from the models tool. For the other workers: a model name their CLI accepts. Omit it to use the worker's configured default (recommended: model names differ between workers).

effort.description: Reasoning effort. For models whose slug ends with a level (e.g. -low, -high), the matching variant of the same model is picked instead.

wait_seconds.description: If > 0, wait up to N seconds (max 600) and return the result directly

name: analyze
description: Ask a worker to read and analyze code in READ-ONLY mode and return a dense summary with path:line references. Use it to save your own context: exploring large codebases, huge files, logs, finding where something is implemented, mapping dependencies, preliminary reviews. Synchronous. Runs in the main repo without auto-approval of tool calls.

question.description: What you want to know, as specifically as possible

worker.description: Worker to use (see the workers tool). Omit it to use the session default or the configured preference order.

fallback.description: If the worker hits a quota/rate limit or its budget is used up, move on to the next worker (default: the fallback setting in the config).

model.description: Model for the chosen worker. For agy: a group (fast, standard, strong, frontier) or an exact slug from the models tool. For the other workers: a model name their CLI accepts. Omit it to use the worker's configured default (recommended: model names differ between workers).

effort.description: Reasoning effort. For models whose slug ends with a level (e.g. -low, -high), the matching variant of the same model is picked instead.

name: jobs
description: Status of delegated jobs. Without job_id: list of the repo's jobs, with the worker that ran each. With job_id: details including the worker's response, earlier attempts (fallback) and the diff. wait_seconds waits for the jobs (or the given one) to finish.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to N seconds (max 600) for the job / all active jobs to finish

include_diff.description: Include the diff in the details (default true)

name: apply
description: Apply a completed job's changes (after reviewing them) to the main repo's working tree, then remove the job's worktree and branch. The changes stay UNCOMMITTED so you can touch them up and test them.

keep_worktree.description: Do not delete the worktree/branch (default false)

name: discard
description: Discard a job (stopping it if running) and delete its worktree and branch.

name: blame
description: Which worker and model wrote a file's lines: matches each line by content against the jobs applied in this repo, so it survives commits, rebases and moved lines; a line edited after the apply counts as not from a worker. Returns compact line ranges with job id, worker/model, date and task title. Use it when a bug lands in code a worker may have written, then reread that job's task.

path.description: File path, relative to the repo root (or absolute)

end.description: Last line, inclusive (default: end of file)

name: workers
description: List the workers with their state: enabled, installed, authenticated (when checkable), budget used/left in the last 24h, active jobs, models, strengths, warnings; plus the preference order, the fallback setting and the session default. With use=<worker> it also sets the default worker for this session ("auto" clears it). With doctor=true it instead checks this system for what isolation and credentials need, and shows the commands to install what is missing (never runs them). Does not use any budget.

use.description: Set the session default worker (a worker id), or "auto" to go back to the configured order. Only when the user asks.

doctor.description: Check the system for isolation and credentials (only for /capocantiere:doctor or when the user asks).

name: mode
description: Show or change the delegation mode, i.e. how much you should delegate to workers: off (tools disabled), manual (only when the user asks), auto (your judgment, the default), prefer (delegate whatever makes sense). There is a global default plus per-repo settings. Without arguments it shows the current mode for this repo. Change it only when the user asks.

mode.description: New mode. "inherit" removes this repo's setting (or, with scope global, goes back to the built-in default).

scope.description: Where to save it: this repo only (default) or the global default.

name: models
description: Models of a worker. For agy (the default here): lists the models the account can use, grouped by capability (fast, standard, strong, frontier, other), shows the defaults for analysis and implementation, and with analyze/implement/exclude changes them (saved across sessions). Other workers don't publish a model list: it shows the configured model. Does not use any budget.

refresh.description: Re-read `agy models` now. Also forgets models marked unavailable after a failed run.

analyze.description: Default model for analyze: a group (follows new models automatically), an exact slug (pinned), or "auto" to go back to the automatic choice.

implement.description: Default model for delegate: a group, an exact slug, or "auto".

exclude.description: Slug patterns (* wildcard) never chosen through a group or by default, e.g. ["claude-*"]. Replaces the current list; [] clears it.
